surveyDefinition.title: Smartwatches — consumer survey (Europe)
surveyDefinition.whatThisSurveyIs: A business-to-consumer (B2C) market research questionnaire about Smartwatches. Every question asks about Smartwatches specifically — not the wider market, not adjacent categories, and not any named brand. It is designed to tell a client what buyers in Europe actually do and want in this category.
surveyDefinition.whoseContextThisIs: Adults in Europe who buy or use Smartwatches for personal or household use. Respondents qualify if they: Owns or intends to purchase a smartwatch within the next 12 months; Uses a compatible smartphone (iOS or Android); Age 18 or older; Able to make purchasing decisions for personal use. Excluded: Children under 18 (unless purchasing for them, but they are not the primary decision-maker); Businesses or institutions purchasing smartwatches in bulk for employees (B2B use); Individuals who only use basic fitness bands without smart features.
surveyDefinition.whyTheseRespondents: Smartwatches are consumer wearable devices purchased by individuals for personal use, fitness tracking, notifications, and health monitoring. While some enterprise or medical applications exist, the primary market is everyday consumers.
respondentBehaviours: Engages in fitness or health tracking activities
Values convenience and connectivity (notifications, calls, payments)
Tends to adopt new technology early or early-majority
May use health apps or fitness wearables
whatIsDeliberatelyNotAsked: Age or household income — these define who was recruited, not what is measured, so they appear in the audience definition rather than as questions.
Brand, company or manufacturer names — the survey stays at category level so findings are not tied to one competitor set.
Where the respondent lives — region is chosen when viewing the results, so asking it again would waste a question.
surveyDefinition.howToReadTheNumbers: Percentages are simulated from a persona-weighted panel of 2,500 synthetic respondents built from real market evidence, not from fieldwork. Single-choice, ranking and rating-scale questions sum to 100%. Multi-select questions do not — each option is an independent share of respondents choosing it. The N shown on each question is the display base for that item.

structure.storyline: Questions run in a planned narrative order: broad and easy first, specific and sensitive last.
structure.storylineSummary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with smartwatches — ownership and usage context — then moves through the purchase journey from triggers and discovery to channel, cycle, decision drivers, and spend. It then explores what they demand from the product, from must-haves to trade-offs and value expectations, and closes with satisfaction, friction, switching triggers, advocacy, and future intent. The arc is progressive: broad and safe at the start, specific and sensitive (money, satisfaction, switching) toward the end.

targetCustomer.summary: Adult consumers of Smartwatches in Europe — who Owns or intends to purchase a smartwatch within the next 12 months; Uses a compatible smartphone (iOS or Android); Age 18 or older; Able to make purchasing decisions for personal use. Smartwatches are a consumer electronics product with a broad demographic appeal. The audience is defined by personal ownership and usage, with emphasis on tech adoption and health/fitness orientation. Excluding bulk B2B purchases keeps the focus on individual consumer behavior.

assumptions: The segment refers to consumer smartwatches (e.g., Apple Watch, Samsung Galaxy Watch, Garmin) rather than specialized medical or industrial wearables.
The survey targets individual consumers, not corporate procurement.
Global scope implies a diverse set of markets, but common consumer behaviors apply.

metadata.storyline_summary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with smartwatches — ownership and usage context — then moves through the purchase journey from triggers and discovery to channel, cycle, decision drivers, and spend. It then explores what they demand from the product, from must-haves to trade-offs and value expectations, and closes with satisfaction, friction, switching triggers, advocacy, and future intent. The arc is progressive: broad and safe at the start, specific and sensitive (money, satisfaction, switching) toward the end.
storyline_notes: For a durable like smartwatches, I dropped the canonical 'repurchase' beat (habitual repurchase is not relevant) and instead emphasized the upgrade/replacement cycle in 'purchase_cycle'.

I added a category-specific 'format_packaging' beat that covers watch size, materials, and band interchangeability, which is critical for smartwatch buyers and maps to the canonical 'format_packaging'.
In buying_behavior, I placed 'decision_drivers' before 'spend' to keep the monetary question last, and I omitted 'repurchase' because smartwatch purchases are infrequent and considered, not routine.
In consumer_profile, I kept the canonical five beats but adapted 'usage_occasion' to include formal vs. sporty contexts, which is relevant for the European market and the style-conscious persona.

In preferences_expectations, I added a 'claims_credentials' beat that includes repairability and sustainability claims, reflecting the Eco-Conscious Minimalist persona and European environmental awareness.

In satisfaction_future_intent, I kept the canonical order but ensured 'switching' is category-level (not brand-level) and placed it after friction, before advocacy and future use, to respect the sensitivity of switching intentions.
metadata.classification_reason: Smartwatches are consumer wearable devices purchased by individuals for personal use, fitness tracking, notifications, and health monitoring. While some enterprise or medical applications exist, the primary market is everyday consumers.
